context.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System provides cataloguing, circulation, and self-service portals for public and academic libraries. It ensures strict EU data residency compliance while delivering high-performance search responses under 800ms.

## Key Elements
* Library Patrons (Members)
* Librarians / Circulation Staff
* Library Administrators
* Library Management System (LMS)
* External Identity Provider (IdP)
* Third-Party Payment Gateway
* Digital Content Repositories

## Relationships
* Patrons, Staff, and Administrators interact with the LMS via HTTPS (TLS 1.3) and API Gateway using OAuth 2.0 / OIDC
* LMS authenticates users with the External IdP using OIDC over HTTPS
* LMS processes fines via Third-Party Payment Gateway using REST/HTTPS with mTLS
* LMS fulfills digital items via Digital Content Repositories using LTI/API

## Technology Stack
* OAuth 2.0 / OIDC: For secure patron and staff authentication and token introspection
* JWT (JSON Web Tokens): For short-lived session management with audience and scope validation
* TLS 1.3 and mTLS: For secure external integrations and transport-layer encryption
* AES-256: For encrypting PII at rest within session caches

## Rationale
This architecture uses an API Gateway and scoped JWTs to enforce strict security and RBAC while supporting offline fallback mechanisms. It meets performance and data residency constraints by keeping all operations and data storage within EU-hosted infrastructure.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System is a comprehensive platform for public and academic libraries to catalogue physical and digital items, manage circulation, and provide self-service portals. It enforces strict EU-only data residency and sub-800ms search performance requirements.

## Key Elements
- Library Patrons (Members), Librarians / Circulation Staff, Library Administrators
- Patron Portal (React.js SPA) and Librarian Back-office (Next.js Web App)
- API Gateway (NGINX / Envoy)
- Catalogue Service (Java/Spring Boot) and Circulation Service (Node.js/Express)
- Asynchronous Event-Driven Messaging (Apache Kafka / RabbitMQ)
- Data Layer: PostgreSQL and Elasticsearch (EU-hosted)
- External Identity Provider (IdP), Third-Party Payment Gateway, Digital Content Repositories

## Relationships
- Patrons and Librarians to Web Frontends via HTTPS
- Web Frontends to API Gateway via HTTPS using OAuth2/OIDC with JWTs
- API Gateway to Backend Services via mTLS via Istio Service Mesh
- Catalogue and Circulation Services to Databases via encrypted connections with AES-256
- Backend Services to Event Broker via TLS-encrypted event streams

## Technology Stack
- React.js / Next.js: For responsive frontends and rapid initial load times
- Java/Spring Boot & Node.js/Express: For decoupled, high-performance backend microservices
- Elasticsearch: EU-hosted search engine ensuring <800ms 99th-percentile search responses
- PostgreSQL: EU-hosted relational database for transactional circulation data
- Apache Kafka / RabbitMQ: Asynchronous messaging to decouple search and check-out workflows
- Istio Service Mesh: For mTLS, zero-trust segmentation, and traffic policies

## Rationale
This architecture decouples heavy patron search traffic from front-desk circulation to protect performance and user experience. It enforces absolute EU data residency and zero-trust security via geo-isolated Kubernetes, regional KMS encryption, and service mesh policies.

Patron Portal.analysis:
## Overview
[The Library Management System provides self-service portals, circulation management, and cataloging for public and academic libraries. It ensures EU data residency compliance and sub-800ms search responses.]

## Key Elements
* Library Patrons (Members)
* Patron Portal (React.js UI SPA & Node.js BFF Server)
* API Gateway (NGINX / Envoy)
* External Identity Provider (IdP)
* Third-Party Payment Gateway
* Catalogue Service & Circulation Service

## Relationships
* Library Patrons -> Patron Portal: Interacts with UI [HTTPS]
* Patron Portal UI -> BFF Server: Communicates via SPA [HTTPS]
* BFF Server -> API Gateway: Proxies API requests [HTTPS/REST, mTLS, OAuth2]
* BFF Server -> External IdP: Manages token exchange [OAuth2/OIDC]
* Patron Portal -> Third-Party Payment Gateway: Processes fines via tokenized iframes [HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
* React.js: UI SPA for patron-facing views ensuring mobile responsiveness
* Node.js / Express: Backend-for-Frontend (BFF) server for secure session management
* HTTP-only, SameSite Cookies: Token storage replacing vulnerable client-side storage
* Stripe Elements / iframes: PCI-DSS scope reduction for payments
* NGINX / Envoy: API Gateway for secure routing

## Rationale
[The BFF pattern secures authentication tokens against XSS while meeting performance and EU data residency constraints. This architecture successfully balances stringent security requirements with low-latency search demands.]

Librarian Back-office.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System provides cataloguing, circulation, and self-service portals for public and academic libraries. It ensures EU-only data residency and sub-800ms search response times.

- Library Patrons, Librarians, Library Administrators

- Circulation Workspace Component, Cataloguing Management Component, Admin Dashboard Component, Auth Session Handler Component
- API Gateway (NGINX / Envoy)

- PostgreSQL Database (EU-hosted), Elasticsearch (EU-hosted)
- External Identity Provider (IdP), Third-Party Payment Gateway

- Librarians / Administrators -> Librarian Back-office: Interacts with application [HTTPS]

- Circulation Workspace Component -> API Gateway: Sends commands and real-time alerts [HTTPS/REST, WebSockets with token authentication]
- Cataloguing Management Component -> API Gateway: Uploads assets [HTTPS/Multipart REST]
- Admin Dashboard Component -> API Gateway: Fetches analytics and reports [HTTPS/REST]

## Technology Stack
- Next.js (React 18+) with Server Actions and App Router: Prevents PII leakage and secures session storage
- HTTP-only, Secure Cookies: Prevents XSS-based token theft
- PostgreSQL & Elasticsearch (EU-hosted): Guarantees data residency and sub-800ms search performance
- OAuth2/OIDC with JWTs: Enforces role-based access control

## Rationale
This architecture uses server-side rendering and isolated frontend components to guarantee strict EU data residency and robust security. It ensures sub-800ms search performance while maintaining strict administrative boundaries and compliance.

API Gateway.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System provides public and academic libraries with item cataloging, circulation management, and self-service portals. It enforces strict EU-only data residency and maintains a 99th-percentile search response time under 800 ms.

## Key Elements
* **Users:** Library Patrons (Members), Librarians / Circulation Staff, Library Administrators
* **Frontends:** Patron Portal (React.js SPA), Librarian Back-office (Next.js Web App)
* **API Gateway:** Envoy / NGINX
* **Backend Services:** Catalogue Service (Java / Spring Boot), Circulation Service (Node.js / Express)
* **Data & Messaging:** PostgreSQL Database (EU-hosted), Elasticsearch (EU-hosted), Distributed Cache (Redis, EU-hosted), Event Broker (Apache Kafka / RabbitMQ)
* **External Systems:** External Identity Provider (IdP), Third-Party Payment Gateway, Digital Content Repositories, EU-hosted SIEM

## Relationships
* Patron Portal -> API Gateway: Sends API requests [HTTPS, OAuth2/OIDC with JWTs]
* Librarian Back-office -> API Gateway: Sends API requests [HTTPS, OAuth2/OIDC with JWTs]
* API Gateway -> Catalogue Service: Routes catalogue queries [mTLS via Istio Service Mesh with SPIFFE/SPIRE]
* API Gateway -> Circulation Service: Routes circulation requests [mTLS via Istio Service Mesh with SPIFFE/SPIRE]
* API Gateway -> External Identity Provider (IdP): Authenticates users and caches JWKs [OIDC over HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
* **API Gateway:** Envoy with WAF filter (ModSecurity), Authentication Filter, Rate Limiting Filter, Route & Load Balancing Engine, Fault Translation & Transformation Filter
* **Caching & Limits:** Distributed Cache (Redis, EU-hosted) for rate limiting quotas
* **Security:** JWT cryptographic verification, Claims Propagation (User ID, Roles in HTTP headers), Zero-Trust mTLS via Istio Service Mesh

## Rationale
Centralizing security, rate limiting, and fault translation at the Envoy API Gateway protects backend services from abuse and guarantees the < 800 ms search latency requirement. Edge-enforced WAF, JWT validation, and mTLS ensure strict compliance with EU-only data residency and zero-trust security mandates.

- Catalogue Service (Java / Spring Boot) containing:
  - Item Controller & Service
  - Search & Indexing Engine
  - Facet & Recommendation Service
  - Digital Content Adapter
  - Event Publisher
- Circulation Service (Node.js / Express)
- Event Broker (Apache Kafka / RabbitMQ)
- PostgreSQL Database (EU-hosted)
- Elasticsearch (Elasticsearch EU-hosted)

## Relationships
- API Gateway -> Catalogue Service: Routes catalogue queries via mTLS using Istio Service Mesh
- Item Controller & Service -> PostgreSQL Database: Reads and writes catalogue data using Spring Data JPA and JDBC with AES-256 encryption
- Search & Indexing Engine & Facet & Recommendation Service -> Elasticsearch: Indexes search data and powers faceted navigation using Spring Data Elasticsearch and Elasticsearch Aggregations API with AES-256 encryption
- Event Publisher -> Event Broker: Publishes domain events via Spring Cloud Stream over TLS
- Digital Content Adapter -> Digital Content Repositories: Fulfills digital items using Spring WebClient over REST/LTI with Resilience4j circuit breakers

## Technology Stack
- Java / Spring Boot: Core runtime for the Catalogue Service providing robust enterprise capabilities
- PostgreSQL: Authoritative relational storage for item metadata secured with AES-256 encryption
- Elasticsearch: High-performance search and aggregation engine ensuring sub-800ms search responses (R-05)
- Spring Data JPA / Spring Data Elasticsearch: Data access layers for relational and search databases
- Resilience4j: Circuit breaker implementation for fault-tolerant external digital repository integrations
- Istio Service Mesh: Secures internal routing with mTLS

## Rationale
This architecture uses a dual-write pattern combining PostgreSQL for authoritative storage and Elasticsearch for high-performance search to meet the strict sub-800ms response time requirement. Furthermore, it enforces EU-only data residency and strict security controls, including AES-256 encryption, OAuth2/JWT RBAC, and PII-free event publishing.

Circulation Service.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System is a solution for public and academic libraries to catalogue items, manage circulation, and provide self-service portals. It enforces strict EU-only data residency requirements.

## Key Elements
- Circulation Service (Node.js / Express container)
- Circulation API Controller (Express.js)
- Loan Management Engine (TypeScript / Domain Services with BullMQ)
- Fine & Payment Manager (Node.js Service with Payment Webhook Handler)
- Event Publisher (KafkaJS Client)
- Data Access Repository (Prisma ORM)
- Notification Scheduler Component (node-cron / BullMQ)
- PostgreSQL Database and Apache Kafka Event Broker

## Relationships
- API Gateway -> Circulation API Controller: Routes circulation requests [mTLS via Istio Service Mesh]
- Data Access Repository -> PostgreSQL Database: Persists circulation data [AES-256 encryption, EU-hosted]
- Event Publisher -> Apache Kafka Event Broker: Publishes check-out and reminder events [TLS-encrypted event streams]
- Fine & Payment Manager -> Third-Party Payment Gateway: Processes fines [REST/HTTPS with mTLS and HMAC webhook verification]

## Technology Stack
- Node.js / Express: Runtime for the Circulation Service ensuring low-latency operations
- TypeScript: Strongly typed domain logic in the Loan Management Engine
- Prisma ORM: Database interactions ensuring secure data access and EU residency compliance
- Apache Kafka: Asynchronous event messaging for decoupled workflows
- BullMQ / node-cron: Background scheduling for automated grace periods and notifications

## Rationale
The component architecture isolates payment processing, event publishing, and loan logic to maintain high performance under 800ms. Strict security controls and decoupled asynchronous tasks ensure GDPR compliance and reliable user experiences.

Event Broker.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System provides item cataloguing, circulation management, and self-service portals for public and academic libraries. It utilizes an asynchronous event-driven architecture to decouple core workflows and guarantee EU-only data residency.

## Key Elements
* Library Patrons (Members) & Librarians
* Patron Portal (React.js SPA) & Librarian Back-office (Next.js Web App)
* API Gateway (NGINX / Envoy)
* Catalogue Service (Java / Spring Boot) & Circulation Service (Node.js / Express)
* Event Broker (Apache Kafka / Confluent Platform, EU-hosted)
* PostgreSQL Database (EU-hosted) & Elasticsearch (EU-hosted)
* Schema Registry & Kafka Streams PII Tokenization App
* Tiered Storage Manager (EU-hosted S3-compatible storage)

## Relationships
* Catalogue Service -> Event Broker: Publishes cataloguing events [mTLS, SASL/SCRAM, TLS-encrypted streams]
* Circulation Service -> Event Broker: Publishes check-out workflows [mTLS, SASL/SCRAM, TLS-encrypted streams]
* Kafka Topics -> Schema Registry: Validates payload schemas on ingestion [HTTPS]
* Kafka Streams -> Elasticsearch: Streams masked projections [Kafka Connect, TLS]
* Event Broker -> Tiered Storage Manager: Offloads historical segments [Encrypted storage]

## Technology Stack
* Apache Kafka: Log-based architecture for replayability, partitioning, and EU data residency.
* Schema Registry: Enforces Avro/Protobuf schemas for backward compatibility and security.
* Kafka Streams: Performs real-time PII tokenization and data masking for GDPR compliance.
* Elasticsearch: Delivers 99th-percentile search response times under 800 ms.
* mTLS & SASL/SCRAM: Secures client connections and enforces topic-level ACLs.

## Rationale
This architecture uses Apache Kafka with strict security and data-masking controls to decouple high-throughput workflows while strictly adhering to EU data residency mandates. The tiered storage and indexing components ensure high-performance self-service operations and rapid search retrieval.

PostgreSQL Database.analysis:
## Overview
[The Library Management System provides cataloging, circulation management, and self-service portals for public and academic libraries. The architecture enforces strict EU-only data residency and high availability while supporting rapid item searches and reliable transactions.]

## Key Elements
* Library Patrons (Members), Librarians / Circulation Staff, Library Administrators
* External Identity Provider (IdP), Third-Party Payment Gateway, Digital Content Repositories
* Patron Portal (React.js SPA), Librarian Back-office (Next.js Web App)
* API Gateway (NGINX / Envoy)
* Catalogue Service (Java / Spring Boot), Circulation Service (Node.js / Express), Event Broker (Apache Kafka / RabbitMQ)
* PostgreSQL Database (Primary Master, Read Replica, PgBouncer, `pg_audit`)
* Elasticsearch

## Relationships
* Patron Portal -> API Gateway: HTTPS/REST [TLS 1.3]
* Librarian Back-office -> API Gateway: HTTPS/REST [TLS 1.3]
* API Gateway -> Catalogue Service: HTTP/gRPC [Internal Network]
* API Gateway -> Circulation Service: HTTP/gRPC [Internal Network]
* Catalogue Service -> PostgreSQL Database (PgBouncer): JDBC/TCP [TLS 1.3, Read-only queries, AES-256]
* Circulation Service -> PostgreSQL Database (PgBouncer): pg driver/TCP [TLS 1.3, Read-write transactions, AES-256]
* Catalogue Service -> Elasticsearch: HTTP/REST [TLS 1.3]

## Technology Stack
* React.js: Powers the Patron Portal for responsive self-service interactions.
* Next.js: Enables server-side rendering for the Librarian Back-office.
* Java / Spring Boot: Chosen for the Catalogue Service to ensure enterprise robustness.
* Node.js / Express: Selected for the Circulation Service for high-concurrency handling.
* PostgreSQL: Manages ACID-compliant circulation and catalogue transactions with EU data residency.
* Elasticsearch: Delivers sub-800ms 99th-percentile search response times.
* PgBouncer & TLS 1.3: Provides connection pooling and secure transport encryption.

## Rationale
[This architecture satisfies EU data residency constraints through localized EU hosting and encrypted storage volumes. It guarantees high availability, ACID compliance, and sub-800ms search performance under peak loads.]
